title: Market Pulse | October 28 Morning: Memory profits meet an energy and policy test
summary: SK Hynix's record profit and long-term memory orders strengthened the AI supply-chain case, but a renewed oil rise, central-bank surprises and tonight's hyperscaler results leave financing and inflation risks unresolved.
reviewed_by: BLAQUE BAUX automated editorial research; independent editorial verification pending

sections.heading: What changed: observed
paragraphs: Tuesday's U.S. session finished with the S&P 500 up 0.60%, Nasdaq Composite up 1.18% and Dow up 0.03%. At 4:53 a.m. ET Wednesday, Nasdaq 100 futures rose 0.41%, S&P 500 futures 0.10%, while Dow futures fell 0.17%. U.S. cash markets were not yet open; futures are an earlier, separately timed snapshot.

SK Hynix reported July-September operating profit of 83.3 trillion won versus 11.4 trillion won a year earlier, beating a 76.7 trillion won analyst estimate. Revenue increased 328% to 104.6 trillion won. The chipmaker announced about 100 trillion won ($75 billion) of planned 2026 shareholder returns and said long-term contracts with 14 customers cover more than half its 2027-2028 production capacity. South Korea's Kospi rose about 6% in Reuters' Wednesday London-session report.

Oil reversed part of Tuesday's easing after a reported Saudi refinery attack. In Reuters' Wednesday London-market snapshot, Brent gained about 1.1% to $115.13 a barrel and European natural-gas futures rose 3.3% to 99.2 euros per MWh. Spot gold declined 0.3% to $4,046.62 at 10:49 GMT in separately timed Reuters reporting.

New Zealand's central bank unexpectedly held its benchmark rate at 2.75%; the New Zealand dollar fell more than 1.3% in Reuters' global-markets account. The STOXX 600 declined 0.25% while U.S. index futures were mixed to modestly higher in that report. Synchronized fresh U.S. Treasury benchmark yields, investment-grade and high-yield spreads, issuer CDS and cash VIX readings were not independently established for this cutoff.

sections.heading: What mattered: interpretation
paragraphs: The material change since Tuesday afternoon is stronger direct evidence of memory-chip pricing power and committed future supply demand. SK Hynix's profit, contracted capacity and shareholder-return plan support supplier economics, but do not establish the eventual return on capital for AI compute customers.

The equity recovery and renewed oil rally pull financial conditions in different directions. Higher energy prices could reinforce inflation concerns even if technology earnings improve; the Reserve Bank of New Zealand surprise illustrates policy divergence rather than a synchronized global easing cycle.

Financing risk should be mapped across chip suppliers, hyperscalers, lenders, leasing vehicles and power infrastructure. A strong supplier income statement does not automatically imply that every downstream project has positive free cash flow. Without synchronized credit-spread data, broad credit improvement or deterioration remains unconfirmed.

sections.heading: What we are watching
list: Federal Reserve decision Wednesday at 2:00 p.m. ET and press conference at 2:30 p.m.: hold versus the tone of inflation and December guidance; distinguish market pricing from an actual decision.
Microsoft and Alphabet earnings after Wednesday's U.S. close: cloud monetization, capital expenditure, operating cash conversion, depreciation, capacity utilization and financing commitments.
Thursday October 29 at 8:30 a.m. ET: BEA advance third-quarter GDP and September personal income and outlays, including PCE inflation.
AI memory supply-chain contracts and margins: SK Hynix HBM allocation, customer concentration, pricing, capacity additions and possible competitive supply.
Actual Gulf export and refinery throughput, Brent and European gas; obtain fresh U.S. Treasury, investment-grade/high-yield spread and VIX readings before inferring cross-asset transmission.

sections.heading: Where we see things going
paragraphs: If hyperscaler results confirm improving cash returns, memory demand stays supported and energy flows normalize, selective technology strength becomes more plausible. That is conditional, not a broad equity forecast.

If energy costs persist and the Fed signals more restrictive policy while credit premiums widen, financing-sensitive AI projects and nontechnology sectors would face a higher risk of underperformance. The available evidence does not support numerical probabilities.

Verification pending: this source-attributed automated edition has not received independent editorial sign-off. Market quotes are historical snapshots, not live prices; current broad credit and volatility readings were not established.

signal: BLAQUE BAUX Signal: SK Hynix validates the supplier side of AI demand; Microsoft and Alphabet must now help validate the customer's cash economics. Watch the financing chain as oil and central-bank risk reprice.
